label: Confirmed Deaths
source: Government/Defensoría del Pueblo tallies (as of Jul 9, 2026)
contestNote: Union and independent sources dispute how many deaths are directly attributable to blockade-caused hospital shortages (~14 of the total) versus other causes.

label: State of Emergency
value: Decree 5707 (90-day extension) approved by ALP, 100-58, Sep 16-17; govt floats possible estado de sitio
contestNote: COB and FENCOMIN both reject the extension as legally unjustified given no active blockades and have each announced (undated) national assemblies to plan a response; the Morales-aligned CSUTCB has separately declared "permanent mobilization" ahead of its own Sep 26 assembly; the government cites the risk of renewed mobilization across ~20 conflict points in 8 departments.
deltaNote: The Legislative Assembly's session, convened by VP Lara for 16:00 on Sep 16, ran past 01:00 on Sep 17 before approving Decree 5707's 90-day extension 100-58 (122 deputies and 36 senators participating), 21 votes above the required threshold. COB executive secretary Mario Argollo and FENCOMIN president Josué Caricari both rejected the measure the same day and each announced a national assembly (ampliado nacional) without setting a date; protesters gathered peacefully at the Casa Social del Maestro near Plaza Murillo during the session with no reported clashes. Separately, the Senate activated a six-member special commission Sep 18 to investigate corruption allegations tied to presidential adviser Fernando Cerimedo, with a three-month mandate.

label: Active Blockades
value: 0 confirmed on the Red Vial Fundamental through Sep 22, but a national 24h transport strike is now set for Mon, Sep 28, with cañeros/arroceros/valle producers and El Alto drivers also threatening indefinite action
source: Administradora Boliviana de Carreteras / Infobae / Los Tiempos, Sep 22-23, 2026
deltaNote: Highways stayed clear through Sep 22, with police and military still guarding Villa Remedios (La Paz-Oruro), Oruro-Cochabamba and El Alto-Tiquina, but pressure built rather than eased: El Alto's driver federation proposed an indefinite strike at its Sep 22 ampliado, cañeros/arroceros/valle producers around Montero (Santa Cruz) gave the government a blockade ultimatum the same day, and on Sep 23 the Confederación Sindical de Choferes de Bolivia (Lucio Gómez) formally called a 24-hour national transport stoppage for Monday, Sep 28, threatening to escalate to an indefinite general strike if unheard.

label: USD Exchange Rate (floated)
source: Central Bank of Bolivia (official TCO, Sep 23, 2026)
deltaNote: Rose from Bs. 11.00 on Sep 20 to Bs. 11.90 on Sep 22 and Bs. 12.06 on Sep 23, resuming its climb after the diesel-subsidy elimination (Decree 5716) and IMF deal ratification, though still below the Sep 9-10 record of Bs. 12.655 struck before the BCB's dollar-distribution interventions.

label: Inflation (y/y)
contestNote: The IMF forecasts full-year 2026 inflation near 20.7%, but Bolivia's statistics institute (INE) reported an official year-on-year print of just 4.93% for July 2026 — pass-through from the June currency float and December fuel-subsidy cuts had not yet fully hit consumer prices.

label: Diesel Price (subsidy fully eliminated)
deltaNote: Decree 5716 replaced Decree 5676's two-tier pricing (Bs. 9.80/L subsidized, Bs. 18.00/L for large 'GRACOS' consumers) with a single international-reference price of Bs. 17.95/L for all consumers, effective Sep 20 — an ~83% jump for previously subsidized transporters, small businesses and individual consumers. Announced hours after Congress ratified the $1.9B IMF financing deal; the government paired it with an expanded PEPE cash bonus (~2.9 million recipients, ~$79M) and Bs. 800 million in preferential credit for transporters and small merchants. Gasoline subsidy decisions were deferred.
contestNote: COB, the Confederación de Choferes, cisterneros (tanker operators) and Yapacaní producers all rejected the decree as an unaffordable 'dieselazo' and moved toward mobilization; the government frames it as an unavoidable IMF condition to end an estimated $55M/week subsidy cost and curb cross-border smuggling.

label: IMF Extended Fund Facility
value: $1.9B ratified by Congress, pending IMF Executive Board (exp. Oct 2)
deltaNote: The Chamber of Deputies approved the 36-month Extended Fund Facility financing law Sep 18 with support well above two-thirds; the Senate sanctioned it via a waived-procedure vote (Law 723) on Sep 19, completing congressional ratification of the SDR 1.369 billion (~$1.9B) program first agreed at staff level Jul 29. Terms: up to 10-year repayment per disbursement, a 4.5-year grace period, and a variable interest rate of 3.47% tied to SDR rates. Final approval from the IMF's Executive Board is expected around Oct 2, with a first disbursement of roughly $250 million anticipated shortly after.

label: Arrests (crisis-related)
contestNote: MAS-aligned and union groups characterize a portion of arrests and the Evo Morales warrant as politically motivated prosecution.

label: Cerimedo-Linked Detentions
value: 4 held + 1 arrest ordered; Cerimedo faces 4 investigations + new Senate probe
source: Attorney General Roger Mariaca / Senate of Bolivia, Sep 9-18, 2026
deltaNote: The Senate activated a six-member, three-party special commission Sep 18 (Paola López and Marcelino Flores of PDC; Leonardo Roca and José Sánchez of Libre; Eliana Acosta and Marcelo Cardona of Unidad) with a three-month mandate to investigate corruption allegations tied to Cerimedo, on top of his four existing criminal matters (illicit enrichment/money laundering, attempted femicide against Nadia Beller, domestic violence, and the Beni drug-trafficking-flights probe). The same day, Beller testified roughly three hours to prosecutors in a Gesell chamber in Santa Cruz, answering ~100 questions, formally requested protected-witness status citing safety fears, and said the Aug 17 attack on her was meant to prevent her from denouncing corruption; a virtual hearing was set for Sep 19 to seek seizure of Cerimedo's digital devices. Cerimedo remains held at the high-security Chonchocoro facility.

label: YPFB State Intervention
source: Government of Bolivia, Supreme Decree 5697, Sep 2, 2026
deltaNote: President Paz placed state oil company YPFB under "extraordinary, transparent and temporary" intervention for up to 180 days (extendable once by 90), via a commission of the Economy, Production/Environment/Water, Hydrocarbons/Energy and Public Works ministries, to audit the fuel import/distribution chain and trace smuggling and diversion networks. The decree does not dissolve YPFB or change its legal status.
